title: Pihennél Egy Kicsit? – Soft Advice With -nál/-nél

sections.title: A gentler way to say it
sections.content: -nél/-nál is the "you" version of the -nék ending you just met: pihennél ("you would rest"), sportolnál ("you would exercise"). Said directly to someone, it works as a gentle suggestion — softer than neked kellene, closer to "you'd rest a bit, wouldn't you?" than a flat instruction.

items.spanish: Pihennél egy kicsit? Nagyon fáradtnak tűnsz.
items.english: Would you rest a little? You seem very tired.

items.spanish: Sportolnál többet? Az jó lenne az egészségednek.
items.english: Would you exercise more? That would be good for your health.

sections.content: This doesn't replace kellene — the two just feel different: neked kellene sounds like advice, while a bare pihennél? sounds like a caring, personal nudge.
